mainEntity.name: How much does a Mercedes S 320 CDI or S 300 CDI engine replacement cost in the UK?

acceptedAnswer.text: A rebuilt OM642 engine for the S 320 CDI costs £2,200-£3,500 supply-only; a rebuilt OM651 engine for the S 300 CDI costs £2,000-£3,000 supply-only. Fitting adds £1,200-£2,500 depending on complexity.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of timing chain failure on a Mercedes S 320 CDI?

acceptedAnswer.text: A rattling noise on cold start or intermittent starting problems are the classic warning signs on the OM642 engine. One owner reported a timing chain failure at only 56,000 miles.

mainEntity.name: Is the Mercedes S 320 CDI engine (OM642) reliable?

acceptedAnswer.text: The OM642 V6 is fundamentally robust, but S 320 CDI owners should be aware of timing chain stretch and oil cooler seal degradation. With these addressed, the engine is capable of 150,000+ miles.

mainEntity.name: How long do Mercedes S 320 CDI and S 300 CDI engines last?

acceptedAnswer.text: Properly maintained OM642 engines routinely reach 150,000-200,000 miles before major work is needed. The OM651 is also durable but requires attention to injector seals.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in my Mercedes S 320 CDI or S 300 CDI?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, if the S Class is otherwise in good condition with no rust or major transmission faults. A rebuilt OM642 costs £2,200-£3,500 - comparable to the value of a £4,000-£12,000 vehicle, making it a justifiable investment for well-maintained examples.

mainEntity.name: What oil does my Mercedes S 320 CDI or S 300 CDI need?

acceptedAnswer.text: Mercedes-Benz specifies low-SAPS oil meeting MB 229.51 - typically 5W-30. The OM642 V6 requires approximately 8.5 litres with filter; the OM651 requires approximately 6.5 litres.

historyTimeline.h2: Mercedes Benz S Class 300/320 CDI - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The S 320 CDI launched with the W221 generation in 2005 as Mercedes' flagship diesel, powered by the OM642 3.0-litre V6 diesel producing 235hp. The S 300 CDI joined the range as an entry-level diesel option, using the same OM642 V6 architecture in a lower-output configuration. In 2009, the S 300 BlueTEC Hybrid introduced the OM651 2.1-litre four-cylinder diesel paired with an electric motor, marking Mercedes' first step into hybrid luxury. The S 320 CDI continued through the W221 lifecycle until 2013, when it was replaced by the S 350 BlueTEC in the W222 generation.

milestones.description: OM642.930, 3.0L V6 diesel, 235hp (S 320 CDI, W221 launch)
OM651, 2.1L four-cylinder diesel hybrid (S 300 BlueTEC Hybrid)
End of W221 production; S 320 CDI replaced by S 350 BlueTEC in W222

historyTimeline.closingNote: Every engine fitted to the Mercedes Benz S Class 300 CDI and 320 CDI is covered below, with UK rebuilt pricing and known failure points - from OM642 timing chain stretch to OM651 injector seal leaks.

commonProblems.h2: Mercedes Benz S Class 300/320 CDI Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The S 320 CDI's OM642 V6 and the S 300 CDI's OM651 four-cylinder are fundamentally robust diesel engines, but both have well-documented weaknesses that become more pronounced with age and mileage. The OM642 is prone to timing chain stretch and oil cooler seal degradation, while the OM651 suffers from injector seal leaks. Every rebuilt engine supplied through EnginesMarket includes upgraded components addressing these original failure points, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.group: OM642 Timing Chain Stretch & Guide Failure
problems.h4: OM642 Timing Chain Stretch & Guide Failure - The S 320 CDI's Most Critical Weakness
problems.typicalFailureMileage: 80,000-120,000 miles (can occur as early as 56,000 miles)
problems.rootCause: The timing chain tensioner can lose hydraulic pressure, allowing the chain to stretch and plastic guides to wear. This is a known issue on the OM642 V6. One owner reported a timing chain failure at only 56,000 miles, requiring a full engine rebuild. Intermittent starting problems have also been traced to stretched timing chains causing cam and crank sensor misalignment.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: STAR diagnostic, cam/crank correlation check, borescope inspection
repairOptions.longevity: First step - confirms whether chain is stretched

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace timing chain, tensioner, guides, sprockets
repairOptions.longevity: 60k-80k miles if caught before chain stretches significantly

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Complete engine swap with upgraded timing components, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: If chain has jumped causing valve damage

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical 2005-2013 S 320 CDI is worth approximately £4,000-£12,000 depending on mileage and condition. These flagship saloons have suffered significant depreciation, meaning replacement costs can approach or exceed vehicle value for higher-mileage examples.
problems.recommendation: If you hear a rattling noise on cold start or experience intermittent starting problems on your S 320 CDI, act immediately. A stretched timing chain on the OM642 can cause catastrophic engine failure. Specialist timing chain replacement at £1,800-£2,800 is significantly cheaper than dealer rates. If the chain has already jumped, a full rebuilt OM642 engine is the only safe option.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt OM642 Mercedes S 320 CDI engine prices

problems.h4: OM642 Oil Cooler Seal Degradation - Coolant Contamination Risk
problems.rootCause: The OM642's oil cooler seals degrade under repeated thermal cycles, allowing oil to leak into the coolant system. This is a labour-intensive repair requiring removal of the intake manifold to access the cooler in the V of the engine.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Remove intake manifold, replace seals, flush cooling system
repairOptions.longevity: If caught early with no other damage

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Complete unit swap with upgraded cooler seals, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: If coolant contamination has caused bearing damage

problems.vehicleValueCheck: As above - a typical S 320 CDI is worth £4,000-£12,000.
problems.recommendation: If you notice milky coolant or oil contamination on your S 320 CDI, have the oil cooler seals inspected immediately. Specialist seal replacement at £950-£1,400 is significantly cheaper than dealer rates. If the engine has been run with contaminated oil, a full rebuilt OM642 is the safer long-term investment.
problems.cta: -> Get quotes for OM642 oil cooler seal replacement & rebuilt engines

problems.h4: OM651 Injector Copper Seal Leak - The S 300 CDI's Common Annoyance
problems.rootCause: The copper sealing washers under the injectors can fail over time, allowing combustion gases to escape past the injector body. The leaking gases bake into a hard, tar-like carbon crust around the injector - known as "Black Death." This creates diesel fumes in the cabin and a messy engine bay.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace copper sealing washer, clean injector bore
repairOptions.longevity: If caught early before injector seizes

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace all four copper sealing washers
Supply & fit rebuilt OM651 with new injectors and seals, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: If injector damage has caused cylinder damage

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical S 300 BlueTEC Hybrid is worth approximately £3,000-£8,000.
problems.recommendation: Injector seal leaks on the OM651 are common but usually not urgent. If you notice diesel fumes in the cabin or see carbon buildup around the injectors, have a specialist inspect the seals immediately. Caught early, resealing an injector is a £120-£250 per cylinder job.
